title: Ops Commander: procedural translator to convert legacy runbooks into task-steps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a translator that turns our corpus of hand-authored runbooks into deterministic, auditable task sequences usable by the Ops Commander UI and the runbook execution service. This will let support engineers run, parameterize, and (optionally) automate remediation flows with RBAC gating and dry-run verification.

What we are shipping: a pipeline that ingests markdown/confluence runbooks, extracts steps and preconditions, annotates safe/unsafe actions, and emits a task JSON that the runner can execute with telemetry hooks. The translator will also produce human-readable diffs for reviewers and an automated canary that runs synthetic checks in the staging tenant.

Progress: prototyping complete (parser + heuristic step tagger). Parser handles 82% of our sampled runbooks without manual edits. Building the canonical task schema now and integrating KV-cache hooks to allow prefix resumption and faster retries. Implemented a first pass feature-flag to keep old manual flow unchanged for teams that opt out.

Decisions and trade-offs: we tried a full NLP intent classifier but reverted to rule-augmented heuristics because classifier drift produced unsafe automatic remediations in early QA. Chosen approach: conservative automation where any ambiguous step is flagged and rendered as a manual confirmation step. This preserves safety while enabling high-confidence automations.

Open risks: permission elevation paths inside some runbooks; we will gate execution behind scoped service accounts and require SSO approval for privileged flows. Another risk: noisy telemetry from synthetic canary runs inflating incident counts; mitigation: a separate synthetic telemetry tag and retention gating in the console.

Links: design doc -> https://confluence.internal.redwood/ops-commander/procedural-translator; initial PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6248; prototype demo recording -> https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/ops-commander-demo.
acceptance_criteria: Translator converts markdown runbooks into canonical task JSON with >= 90% step coverage on validation set
Generated tasks include explicit quiesce/checkpoint points and do not contain unapproved privilege escalation actions
Translator outputs a human diff view and auto-links to related telemetry queries and runbook owner
Ops Commander UI can import translated tasks and run them in dry-run mode without executing destructive steps
End-to-end telemetry: each translated task run produces a trace and token-level cost estimate visible in Console
steps: Finalize canonical task schema and publish in design doc
Add conservative heuristics for ambiguous actions and mark them manual-by-default
Integrate translator with KV cache hooks and the runner API for resumable runs
Wire up RBAC gating and SSO approval flow for privileged steps
Create synthetic canary suite for staging runs and add synthetic telemetry tag
Ship PR and rollout behind feature flag; run opt-in pilots with SRE and Customer Support
comments: 2025-02-19 | Claire Nguyen: Reviewed prototype results. Parser coverage looks promising but we need a clearer UX for flagged ambiguous steps (recommend inline explanation and suggested fallbacks).
2025-02-26 | Diego Morales: Implemented suggestion: ambiguous steps now render a suggested subtask with a one-click escalate-to-manual button in UI. Pushed updated parser rule-set (see PR #6248).

2025-03-01 | SRE Oncall (Jordan Lee): Ran synthetic canary against staging; one runbook caused a permission escalation attempt. Added requirement: translator must surface 'requires-sudo' tag and block automation unless explicit approval exists.
2025-03-04 | Aisha Patel: Prioritized RBAC gating. Marking security review as requested and scheduling a sync with Security for 2025-03-10.
notes: We will maintain a migration dashboard listing translated runbooks and their pilot status for owners to review.
If translator mislabels a step, owners can submit a quick correction which will re-run the translation and update the diff automatically.
Plan to run a 2-week pilot with SRE and CS starting 2025-03-20; monitor false-positive rate and human override frequency.
